newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.

text.p: Carryover selling from limit losses Tuesday were expected to pressure CME hog futures for losses of 0.100 to 0.300 cent per lb early and pork bellies were seem dropping 0.300 to 0.800 cent, livestock analysts said.

Adding to pressure in hog futures were indications of mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower cash hog markets as cooler weather moved into major hog producing areas, making transporting of hogs easier. Weight gains were also expected to rise on the cooler weather, they said.
Analysts also continued to voice concern the recently expected pick-up in pork exports to Japan has not been as large as expected. The seasonal trend for pork also is down in domestic markets.

Pork bellies also were likely to be pressured by limit losses on Tuesday with fundamentals pointing lower. Demand for product waned when cash belly prices reached the $90 per cwt level and were seen working lower, especailly in light of increased production, sources said.

Tuesday's CME out-of-town report, although in line with most expectations, was viewed as mildly bearish to futures. The reduction in stocks, at 3,416,000 lbs, should have been larger in view of the light pace of hog slaughter last week, some sources said.
